description: Single-panel schematic temperature–time process-route diagram (no drawn axes, no scale bar) summarising production variants for hot rolled and cold rolled austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steel strips. The left branch begins at a slab-reheating plateau labelled "1100-1200°C" and descends through a serrated "HR" hot-rolling symbol with "FRT 900°C" printed on the slope, then splits into a dashed fast-cooling path and a solid path dropping to a serrated "CR" cold-rolling symbol. The right branch carries plateaus labelled "900-1100°C Solution" and "600-900°C Annealing", with dash-dot "Aging" curves at the far right. Five numbered routes (1-5) with downward arrows distinguish the variants: process 1, dashed, is fast cooling to 500-750°C then slow cooling or isothermal holding; process 2 is fast cooling to room temperature followed by isothermal annealing; processes 3, 4 and 5 are cold-rolled paths in which strip is solution treated at 900-1100°C, quenched, then aged — process 3 without isothermal holding, 4 and 5 arranged to maximise age hardening. The panel demonstrates that one Fe-Mn-Al-C composition can be routed to hot-rolled or cold-rolled, age-hardenable or non-age-hardenable products through the choice of cooling, coiling and annealing schedule.

observations.observation: The schematic is drawn as a temperature–time route diagram with the reheating plateau labelled "1100-1200°C" on the far left and "FRT 900°C" printed on the hot-rolling slope.
A serrated/zigzag symbol labelled "HR" marks the hot-rolling step and a second serrated symbol labelled "CR" marks the cold-rolling step at low temperature.
The central plateaus of the diagram are labelled "900-1100°C Solution" and "600-900°C Annealing", and the right-hand dash-dot family of curves is labelled "Aging".
Five numbered routes are printed in the diagram: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, each terminating in a downward arrow indicating continued cooling or an end of treatment.
Route 1 is drawn as a dashed curve that leaves the hot-rolled state without passing to room temperature and continues to the right-hand side of the diagram.

The caption states that the figure shows process variants for producing hot rolled and cold rolled austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steel strips and that the numbers identify process routes described in the text.
The citing text states that for hot rolled products the strip can be fast cooled after hot rolling to 500–750 °C and then slow cooled or isothermally held, corresponding to process 1.
The citing text states that the hot rolled strip can alternatively be fast cooled to room temperature and then isothermally annealed, corresponding to process 2.

The citing text states that the cooling rate after hot rolling should be high enough to avoid formation of intergranular κ-carbides, and that coiling temperature and cooling rate can target nanoscale κ-precipitates while overaging must be avoided.

The citing text states that cold rolled strips of age-hardenable austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels are solution treated at 900–1100 °C in the single austenite phase area and then quenched in water, oil or other quench media.
The citing text states that process 3 has no isothermal holding and that processes 4 and 5 are applied to maximise the age hardening effect of κ-phase precipitation.
The citing text states that the common age-hardening practice is an isothermal hold of 5–20 h in the temperature range 500–700 °C.

The citing text states that for non-age-hardenable austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, recovery or recrystallisation annealing at 600–900 °C for a short time of 1–5 min can be applied after cold rolling to restore ductility or refine grains.

subfigures.description: Plateau labelled "1100-1200°C" (slab reheating) followed by a descending line with the serrated "HR" deformation symbol and "FRT 900°C" written on the slope, i.e. finish rolling temperature 900°C.
After hot rolling the line splits into a dashed fast-cooling path running to the right and a solid path descending to a serrated "CR" symbol marking cold rolling at near-ambient temperature.
Dashed curve continuing from the hot-rolled state toward the right into the Aging region; the caption/citing text assign it fast cooling to 500-750°C followed by slow cooling or isothermal holding.
Solid curve (labelled 2) descending to an isothermal hold then an arrow downward; the citing text identifies it as fast cooling to room temperature followed by isothermal annealing.
Upper plateau labelled "900-1100°C Solution" and lower plateau labelled "600-900°C Annealing", representing solution treatment in the single austenite phase field and subsequent annealing.

Three curves labelled 3, 4 and 5 leaving the solution-treatment plateau with downward arrows; process 3 shows no isothermal hold, while 4 and 5 extend into the dash-dot "Aging" curves at the far right.

unreadable_items: No x-axis (time) and no y-axis (temperature) scale is drawn: the time extent of each route is not quantified in the figure itself and the printed temperature ranges are the only numeric anchors.
The exact shapes/undercooling of the dashed route-1 curve and the dash-dot aging curves are schematic only; no numeric values are printed on the curves.
